clue.text: Soldier letting go of prisoner's hand

indicators.note: to let go of something is to release it, so a part of the first word is dropped

parts.note: a conscript is a soldier called up for service
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A guard releases a captive's hand from his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSCRIPT loses CON to leave SCRIPT. 'Hand' here is handwriting, not the body part the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's hand is their style of handwriting, which is also called their script.

clue.text: Position that offers opportunities for training?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a post or place
second meaning, cryptic: the place where you catch a train

explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like coaching or education, but the question mark points to boarding trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is both an assigned post or rank and a stop where trains pick up passengers.

clue.text: Bottled beer and lager to begin with are revolting

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what something begins with is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bottled beer and lager are disgusting, at least at first taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgusting, but the definition means rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are revolting are rising against authority, so they rebel; both are plural verbs.

clue.text: Does Pablo dance this?

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and swap places

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a Spaniard called Pablo performs this dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the Spanish-styled dance is just what a Pablo might dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a fast ballroom dance modelled on a Spanish bullfight march.

clue.text: They author legal documents framing employer's case

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the documents surround the other letters

parts.note: writs are formal court orders

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Lawyers draft paperwork that sets out an employer's side of a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal case, which suits the surface, but it means the outer shell of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers are the people who author books and other works, so they author things by trade.

clue.text: Eliminate small uncertainty for auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small, and a doubt is an uncertainty

explanation.surface: A minor doubt raised by someone checking the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it just means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed out is to remove unwanted members of a group, the way weeds are pulled.

clue.text: Make stronger guarantee to eliminate source of stress

indicators.note: eliminating something takes it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss

indicators.note: the source of something is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Make a promise sturdier by removing what causes the worry.
explanation.walkthrough: INSURE loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to toughen them so they can endure hardship, hence make them hardier.

clue.text: Former partner turned corruption into crooked money-making scheme

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: something turned has been twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rot is decay or moral corruption
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ex-partner who turned to corruption and ran a crooked scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link word, but its letters join ROT in the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining money through threats or force, a criminal way of making money.

clue.text: Delivery of first letter from postbag in school

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation
the first letter is P, written out as a word

explanation.surface: Getting the first letter out of the school mailbag.
explanation.walkthrough: SCH holds PEE, the spelt-out name of the letter P. 'Delivery' looks like the post, but means how one speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's or speaker's delivery is their way of talking, their speech.

clue.text: Ken's partner is rather spiky we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound

parts.note: barby, like barbed, means somewhat prickly

explanation.surface: Gossip that someone's partner is rather prickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is the boyfriend doll of the famous Mattel fashion doll.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbie is the doll whose boyfriend in the toy range is Ken.

clue.text: Surprise attack clipped trainee soldier on American vehicle

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end trimmed off, so the last letter goes
in a down clue, being on something means sitting after it, so the soldier comes second

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a bus is a vehicle
a cadet is a soldier in training

explanation.surface: A young recruit riding on a US army truck is caught in an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambuscade is an archaic word, borrowed from Spanish emboscada.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an old word for an ambush, an attack sprung from hiding.

clue.text: Free to marry once it has been put back

indicators.note: to put something back is to turn it the other way round

parts.note: marrying two people unites them
the two letters of this word inside the previous one are the ones to turn round

explanation.surface: A divorcee is free to wed again once the matter has been settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the 'it' inside the verb is turned round; the rest stays in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to release or loosen it, so free is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Vain daughter did very little

parts.note: an idle boast or threat is a vain one, without effect
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A conceited girl who does almost nothing all day.
explanation.walkthrough: Vain here means futile, as in an idle threat, not conceited as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To have idled is to have lazed about, doing very little.

clue.text: Life story in verse based on physical characteristics

parts.note: a bio is a short biography
metric verse is written in metre

explanation.surface: A biography written as a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Biometric data measures bodily features such as fingerprints or faces.

clue.text: Remarkable decision not to approve board

parts.note: a no is a refusal
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A striking refusal by a company's board to give its approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like the directors who decide, but it is just a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is worth noting, hence remarkable or striking.

clue.text: Management team swimming in river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river

indicators.note: swimming things move around freely, so these letters change places

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The bosses take the whole team for a swim in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a river in the English Midlands. 'Management' looks like the bosses but means handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the way something is handled or dealt with, which is a sense of management.

clue.text: Blurring of CGI and art could be disastrous

indicators.note: blurring smears the lines, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mixing computer graphics with traditional art might end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: CGI is computer-generated imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic outcome is a calamitous one, so the word is a synonym of disastrous.

clue.text: Carved stone in style of baroque breast

parts.note: à la is French for in the style of

indicators.note: baroque means ornate and convoluted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sculpted stone bust in the baroque manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white mineral prized by sculptors for carving ornaments and statues.

clue.text: Resounding effect of Britain always recalled

indicators.note: to be called back is to come back the way it went, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: standard abbreviation
ever means at all times, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at how Britain always made an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: BR plus EVER, read backwards, gives REVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb is short for reverberation, the echoing sound effect used in music production.

clue.text: Spooner's musical obsession is something quite breathtaking?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: Hair is a rock musical, and a bug is a craze or obsession

explanation.surface: An obsession with musicals described as quite breathtaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of HAIR BUG. The question mark flags that 'breathtaking' is literal: a tight squeeze stops your breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a crushing embrace, so it literally takes your breath away.

clue.text: Not in favour of encore by soprano and tenor

parts.note: an encore is a call to perform once more
standard abbreviation in music
standard abbreviation in music

explanation.surface: A disapproving audience member objects to another encore from two singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means opposing it, the opposite of supporting it.

clue.text: Call father informally about distant relative?

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
pa is a casual word for dad

explanation.surface: Someone affectionately calls their dad a far-off kinsman.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME PA is read backwards. The question mark warns the relative is distant in evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An apeman is a primitive human ancestor, a very remote member of the human family tree.

clue.text: What may help some people receiving criticism?

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: they refers to some people in general
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A question about what might help people who are being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague; the question mark signals that therapy is just one example of help.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve, so it is something that may help.

clue.text: Trucks used to be circling ground regularly

indicators.note: circling something means going around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: was is the past form of be

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Lorries that once drove round and round a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a stadium in the surface, but only its odd letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons are railway goods trucks or other freight vehicles, so trucks is a synonym.

clue.text: Every other change had to involve chairperson in the end

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to alter is to change
had a meal, so ate

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rule change meant the chair had to be involved by the end of every other meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTER, then ATE holding N, gives ALTERNATE. 'Had' as in had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate days are every second day, skipping one between each, so every other.

clue.text: King is greeting wise man from the East

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: A monarch greets one of the Magi arriving from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise man from the East' suggests the Magi of the Nativity, but means an Indian sage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or seer, an inspired holy poet from Indian tradition.

clue.text: Stroll went all over the place except outside

indicators.note: everything except the outside means the outer letters are left off

parts.note: to ramble is to wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: A walker wandered everywhere except outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMBLED drops its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, so stroll is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Live group attacked from all directions

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A band playing live is mobbed from every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective for a music gig, but it is the verb meaning exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means surrounded or harassed on all sides, by enemies or troubles.

clue.text: Person wanting right to run sporting events

indicators.note: letters that run like a ladder in tights come apart and reform
wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone who wants the right to stage sports tournaments.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSON loses R, and the remaining five letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Opens are tournaments, notably in golf and tennis, open to amateurs and professionals alike.

clue.text: I'm surprised about the Alps new resort

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the rest

parts.note: ha! is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to hear of a new holiday destination in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: HA goes around a rearrangement of THE ALPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A health spa is a place people visit to relax and get fit, a kind of resort.

clue.text: Group of people eating in office

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a session of a meal served to one batch of diners
second meaning: currently holding a post

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests staff having lunch in the office; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner sitting is one round of diners, and a sitting member is one currently serving.

clue.text: Fair game must accept empty threat

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: game is hunted animals, so prey

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sportsman must put up with a hollow threat in a fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is the hunted kind, not a match, and 'Fair' is the definition rather than describing the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means good-looking, so pretty is a synonym.
